The Glenn-HT code is based on the TRAF3D code and uses the full compressible Navier-Stokes equations.
The code employs a multi-stage Runge-Kutta scheme to march in pseudo time and uses multi-grid and implicit residual smoothing to accelerate convergence.
The k-ω turbulence model used in the code does not require the computation of wall distance y+, which is advantageous for handling complicated geometries.
The code has been used to simulate a variety of flows including turbine blades, tip clearance flows, film cooling holes, and coolant channels.
Experimental and numerical studies on rib roughened channels with and without rotation are discussed, providing context for the current work.
The MWD algorithm is able to reduce the initial number of blocks by 50-90% on average for complex test cases.
The MWD chooses which internal face to remove to minimize the number of other candidates that are disqualified, thus depleting the set of candidates at the slowest rate.
Repeated application of the MWD increases the likelihood of realizing the actual minimum number of blocks for a given geometry.
The MWD is a fully 3D algorithm that uses only connectivity data, requiring very little memory.
The final number of blocks produced by the MWD is close to the expected minimum in most cases tested.
